newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan invites bids to export 33,500 T rice.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan invites bids to export 33,500 T rice.

text.p: The state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP) said on Monday it had invited tenders on August 29 for the sale and export of 2,500 tonnes of basmati Pak-7 rice and 30,988 tonnes of IRRI-6 rice.

An RECP official said the rice, from the 1995/96 crop (July-June), was currently stored in warehouses near Port Qasim and other locations. Bids must be submitted by 1700 GMT on August 29 and would be opened immediately.
He said the basmati Pak-7 contained seven percent broken while the IRRI-6 was in six different lots containing 10 to 45 percent broken.
In the last tender issued in June, RECP sold 2,500 tonnes of basmati Pak-7 at $441 per tonne FOB.
Pakistan exported 1.717 million tonnes of rice worth $460 million in 1996/97 (July-June), compared to 1.6 million tonnes worth $504 million in 1995/96.
In June, rice exports fell to 86,488 tonnes worth $28 million compared to 151,568 tonnes worth $39 million in May and 347,471 tonnes worth $93 million in June 1996.
